newsitem.title: CHINA: China declines comment on HK troops plan.
newsitem.headline: China declines comment on HK troops plan.

text.p: China's Ministry of Defence on Friday declined to comment on a statement by the office of Hong Kong's future leader that Beijing would send 4,000 troops into the territory on the first day of Chinese rule on July 1.

The statement from the office of Hong Kong's Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said China would send helicopters, ships and armoured vehicles into Hong Kong six hours after Beijing returns the colony to Beijing.
Ministry of Defence officials maintained their tradition of secrecy, declining to make any comment on their plans for deploying the territory's first post-colonial garisson.
"We don't know anything about this," said one official of the ministry's foreign affairs bureau.
China's People's Liberation Army already has 196 advance troops in Hong Kong and another 509 are to join them shortly before the handover ceremony at midnight (1600 GMT) on June 30.

Outgoing Governor Chris Patten denounced Beijing's decision to send the 4,000 troops just hours after the midnight June 30 handover, saying it would send the wrong kind of signal to the international community and the people of Hong Kong.
